title: Joyagoo Link Not Working? Check the Original Product URL
description: Fix a Joyagoo product link that will not open: separate a broken spreadsheet link, login wall, unavailable variant and import error before ordering.
sourceNote: Reviewed 13 October 2026. An independent troubleshooting method for product discovery; examples are illustrative. Account screens and seller availability may change.
quickFacts: Keep the original URL before changing anything
A login wall does not prove a product is deleted
Check the exact variant, not only the main image
Treat a replacement listing as a new candidate

sections.heading: Find the point where the link stops working
paragraphs: When a Joyagoo link is not working, first identify which link failed. A spreadsheet row may open an independent catalog, that catalog may point to a seller page, and the seller URL may then be imported into the buying platform. These are separate steps. An error at one step does not establish that the product has disappeared from every other step. Copy the spreadsheet address, the link you clicked and the final address shown in your browser into a private research note.

Write down the visible outcome: blank page, sign-in request, product not found, unrelated product, missing size or an import message. Include the time and the device you used. This small record prevents random changes from obscuring the original problem. Do not place a second order simply because a page fails to load; first check whether an earlier payment or order already exists in your account.

sections.heading: Recover the seller URL without guessing an identifier
paragraphs: Reopen the row and look for an explicitly supplied source link or product identifier. A catalog address identifies the catalog entry; it is not automatically a Taobao, Weidian or 1688 product address. If a share link opens successfully, use the product page's own sharing option to obtain a fresh link. Keep the old and new versions so you can compare the destination. Remove surrounding copied sentences or punctuation from the input field, but preserve the actual link.

Do not delete every query parameter. On some marketplaces, the query contains the product ID, so cutting the URL at the question mark can remove the very information needed to retrieve it. Do not invent an item ID from a filename, an image or a similar row. If only a screenshot survives, image search can produce new candidates, but every result needs a new identity and variant check. Visual similarity does not restore the original seller relationship.

sections.heading: Distinguish an access problem from a removed product
paragraphs: A marketplace may show a login screen, an app prompt or a regional access message before displaying product details. Record that as access unresolved. It is not sufficient evidence to mark the product sold out. If you already use the marketplace, open its normal site or app and inspect the saved source link there. Enter credentials only through the service's genuine sign-in flow, never into a form on an unrelated spreadsheet or a page sent by an unknown commenter.

A clear unavailable message on the seller page is different. Check whether the whole listing is gone or only the selected option. A jacket can remain visible while the blue medium variant is unavailable. If a page redirects to a store homepage, it has not confirmed the old product. A successful page load is therefore only the beginning of the check; the relevant item and option still need to be present.

sections.heading: Handle a working seller page that will not import
paragraphs: If the original product page is accessible but the buying platform cannot retrieve it, the evidence points to a retrieval problem rather than a confirmed product deletion. Try the fresh seller link once, then preserve the error instead of repeatedly submitting copies. Joyagoo's public shopping guidance mentions manual DIY orders when normal product retrieval is unavailable. Check the current official workflow and its requirements before using that route.

A manual entry transfers more responsibility to your notes. Record the source URL, seller, exact option text, quantity, currency, visible price and domestic delivery information. Ask for clarification where the seller page is incomplete. A manually typed description does not reserve stock or make an unsupported option available. Do not pay while the intended size, color or quantity remains ambiguous, and do not bypass an item restriction by describing a different product.

sections.heading: Compare the recovered page against the saved row
paragraphs: Place the spreadsheet thumbnail and the recovered listing side by side. Compare product type, shape, visible details, seller information and any stable identifier. Then select the intended option and inspect its image and price. The main image may show a bundle while the lowest displayed price applies to a single component. A recovered link is usable only after this option-level check, not simply because its title contains the same words.

Consider an illustrative shoe row saved with a black low-top thumbnail. The new page uses the same image but offers only a different sole design in the required size. That is a partial match, not a repaired order instruction. Keep it out of the ready-to-buy list until the difference is resolved. If a replacement seller has the desired design, create a new record with a new check date rather than silently attaching it to the old entry.

sections.heading: Send a support request that can be reproduced
paragraphs: A useful report includes the spreadsheet row address, original seller URL, final destination, exact option and a short description of the failure. Add the time, browser or app, and a screenshot with personal details hidden. For an import issue, state that the seller page opens but the buying platform does not retrieve it. For a wrong destination, state which visible product detail differs. This gives the recipient a concrete check to perform.

Keep account IDs, delivery addresses and payment screenshots out of public comments. If an existing order is involved, use the platform's authenticated support channel and the relevant order reference. A report about a stale independent catalog entry belongs with that catalog's maintainer; a payment or purchased-order issue belongs with the service handling the transaction. Separating these responsibilities avoids asking the wrong party to fix a problem it cannot control.

sections.heading: Use a clear stop-or-continue decision
paragraphs: Continue only when the final destination identifies the intended product, the required variant is available to select, and the order summary agrees with your saved note. Stop when the source cannot be identified, the page has changed product, a required detail is missing or the error leaves an earlier order's state uncertain. A screenshot of a past price is useful history, but it does not establish today's availability or authorize a different item.

Update the spreadsheet record with the result: working and matched, access unresolved, variant unavailable, wrong destination or removed listing. Add a real check date only after reviewing the page. If you found an alternative, retain it as a separate candidate. This turns one frustrating broken link into better research data and makes the next search faster without inventing certainty about a seller, product or future delivery.

title: Joyagoo Size Chart Guide: Measure Before Choosing a Size
description: Compare seller size charts with clothes that fit. Check chest width, length, waist and inseam, then write a precise measurement request for your Joyagoo order.
sourceNote: Reviewed 13 October 2026. Practical measurement guidance, not a universal brand conversion chart. Numerical examples are illustrative; the selected seller's chart controls the listing.
quickFacts: There is no single size chart for every seller
Compare garment measurements with garment measurements
Keep units and measuring points consistent
A printed size label alone does not confirm fit

sections.heading: Start with a reference garment, not a familiar letter
paragraphs: Searching for a Joyagoo size chart usually begins with a simple question: which size should I select on this product link? The useful answer comes from the individual seller's measurements. A familiar M, L or EU label is only a label until you know the cut and dimensions behind it. Save the chart from the exact listing and check whether it describes the selected style, a different item in the same listing or body measurements rather than clothing.

Choose a garment you already wear comfortably and that serves the same purpose. Compare a hoodie with a hoodie of similar thickness, not with a thin T-shirt. Lay it flat without stretching it, smooth obvious folds and use a flexible tape. Record the measuring points as well as the numbers. This makes your reference repeatable and gives a warehouse measurement request a clear meaning later.

sections.heading: Read the units and the measurement type
paragraphs: Check whether the chart uses centimeters or inches before comparing numbers. One inch equals 2.54 centimeters. Also distinguish flat width from circumference. A chest measurement of 56 cm across a laid-flat garment is not the same field as a 56 cm chest circumference. If a chart calls both fields chest without a diagram, ask which method was used. Do not resolve an unclear field by simply doubling or halving it until a size looks plausible.

Record whether the seller gives a garment measurement, a suggested body measurement or a height-and-weight recommendation. These can support different decisions and should not share one column. A height-and-weight table cannot tell you sleeve length, shoulder shape or the amount of room at the waist. Fabric stretch, lining and the intended silhouette can also change comfort at the same nominal measurement, so keep those observations beside the chart.

sections.heading: Measure tops at consistent points
paragraphs: For a T-shirt or sweatshirt, measure chest width from underarm to underarm with the garment flat. Record body length from the same chosen starting point on every garment, such as the high shoulder point beside the collar. Note whether the seller measures from that point or from the back collar instead. For set-in sleeves, shoulder seam to cuff and shoulder seam to shoulder seam can help, but a dropped shoulder or raglan sleeve needs a matching diagram.

Use the reference garment to identify your priorities. A cropped fit may make body length the decisive field; a fitted jacket may make chest room and shoulder mobility more important. Do not average incompatible measurements into a single size score. If the chest works but the sleeve would be too short, the listing may be a poor match even when one of its labels normally fits you. The best choice can be another cut rather than the next letter size.

sections.heading: Measure trousers and shoes using their own conventions
paragraphs: For trousers, note waist width, rise, inseam and thigh width where the seller provides them. State whether an elastic waist is measured relaxed or stretched. Measure inseam from the crotch seam to the hem along the inside leg. Keep front rise separate from total length: two trousers with the same outer length may fit differently because their rise differs. Compare against a reference pair with a similar intended waistband position.

For shoes, do not assume that a printed EU or US size converts identically across sellers. Check whether a stated centimeter value means recommended foot length, insole length or another dimension. These are not interchangeable. Measure both feet while standing and use the larger relevant measurement for your comparison, while also considering width and the type of sock you expect to wear. A warehouse photo of an outsole does not automatically establish the internal space available to your foot.

sections.heading: Work through a comparison before selecting the variant
paragraphs: Imagine that a comfortable hoodie measures 58 cm across the chest and 68 cm in body length using your recorded method. The seller lists M at 56 and 67 cm, and L at 59 and 70 cm. L is closer on chest width but two centimeters longer than the reference. That does not make it universally correct. Decide whether the added length is acceptable and check any other critical measurement before choosing. These numbers are an example, not a recommendation for a real product.

A helpful comparison record has five fields: measurement name, reference value, seller value, difference and decision. Keep any seller-stated tolerance separate. If no tolerance is given, mark it unknown rather than inventing a standard allowance. A small difference may be acceptable in a relaxed garment and significant in a fitted one. Write your own acceptable range before purchase so you can make a consistent decision when actual measurement evidence arrives.

sections.heading: Write a measurement request someone can follow
paragraphs: Replace a vague request such as check the size with a specific instruction: photograph the hoodie flat, show the tape from underarm seam to underarm seam without stretching, and include both ends of the tape in the frame. For body length, name the starting point and ask for the whole measuring path. Include the order item and selected size so the request cannot easily be applied to a different product in the same parcel.

Confirm whether the current service offers the requested measurement, whether it costs extra and when it can be completed. A request is not proof that the measurement has already happened. On receipt, check that the tape is readable, the item is not folded across the measuring line and the units are visible. If the image does not answer the question, ask for the missing evidence while the relevant order options are still available.

sections.heading: Keep the size record through the QC decision
paragraphs: Save the source URL, selected option text, chart image, reference measurements and date together. When warehouse photos arrive, compare the label with the ordered variant first, then compare measured dimensions using the same method. A correct label can still leave a fit concern unresolved; conversely, an unfamiliar label may accompany measurements that match the seller's chart. Describe the actual discrepancy instead of claiming that every item with that label must fit the same way.

Decide between keeping, requesting clarification or pursuing an available after-sales option using the evidence and current seller terms. Do not assume that a sizing preference guarantees a return or that a photo can prove comfort in motion. Record what remains uncertain. The goal of the size-chart process is to make the variant choice more informed and easier to check, not to promise a perfect fit from a generic conversion table.

title: Joyagoo QC Photos: Compare Your Item With the Listing
description: Check Joyagoo QC photos against the exact product option you ordered. Identify missing evidence and write useful requests for labels, measurements and close-ups.
sourceNote: Reviewed 13 October 2026 against Joyagoo's published quality-check scope. The comparison method and request examples are independent editorial guidance.
quickFacts: Start with the saved order option
A missing view is an open question, not a confirmed defect
Ask for a specific angle or measurement
Photos do not establish authenticity or hidden performance

sections.heading: Build a comparison from three separate records
paragraphs: To review Joyagoo QC photos use three records: the seller listing you saved, the option shown in your order and the warehouse images of the received item. Each answers a different question. The listing describes an offer, the order records what was selected, and the photographs show visible aspects of one received unit. Mixing these records can make an ordinary variant difference look like an error, or hide a real mismatch behind an attractive product image.

Before enlarging details, confirm that you are viewing the right order item. A warehouse account may contain several similar shirts or two sizes of one shoe. Keep the order reference in your private notes and compare the corresponding photo set only. If a photograph cannot be confidently associated with the correct item, resolve that first. A detailed review of the wrong photo set produces a precise-looking but useless conclusion.

sections.heading: Check identity and selected options before workmanship
paragraphs: Start with the product family, color, size label, model or version, quantity and included parts. Compare these with the exact option text, not just the seller's main thumbnail. Listings often use a representative picture for several variations. A bag photographed with a strap or an accessory does not establish that every option includes it. Preserve the selected option's description so you can identify whether a missing part was actually promised.

Use one line for each finding: expected, visible and unresolved. For example, expected two pieces, visible one piece, unresolved whether the second piece is outside the frame. That wording identifies the next useful check without prematurely asserting that the warehouse or seller lost something. If the photo clearly shows the wrong printed size relative to the order, save the relevant image and describe the mismatch directly rather than adding unrelated judgments about overall quality.

sections.heading: Inspect visible condition without overclaiming
paragraphs: Look for visible tears, stains, broken components, uneven alignment and obvious damage to the item or required accessories. View the full image first so you retain context, then enlarge the area of concern. A dark patch may be a shadow or a surface mark; compression can make stitching look less clear than it is. Record the observation and request a closer view where the image cannot distinguish between plausible explanations.

Joyagoo's published QC scope describes visual checks with limits. Treat a photograph as evidence of what it visibly shows, not as a certificate of authenticity, durability or internal performance. A clean exterior on an electronic item does not demonstrate that it powers on. A straight-looking seam does not establish long-term strength. If a hidden characteristic matters to your purchase, identify what evidence or service would actually be needed rather than assuming the standard photo set covers it.

sections.heading: Ask for extra photos that answer one decision
paragraphs: A useful extra-photo request names the item, area, angle and purpose. For a label: please take one close-up with the whole size and composition label readable. For a suspected mark: please photograph the left sleeve in even light, then provide a close-up of the marked area. For an accessory: please show all included pieces together beside the main item. These requests are more actionable than more photos please because the missing information is explicit.

Prioritize requests that could change your decision. If you would keep the item regardless of a decorative detail, it may be less urgent than checking the required size or a possible broken fastener. Confirm current availability and any charge before requesting optional work. Avoid asking for several near-identical angles simply to make the photo set look complete. The aim is to close a specific evidence gap while leaving enough time to act on the answer.

sections.heading: Use measurements to resolve fit uncertainty
paragraphs: A visible M or L label confirms a printed label, not the dimensions of the garment. If chest width or length is decisive, request a photo with a tape placed along a defined path. Name the starting and ending points, require a flat unstretched item and ask for both tape ends to remain visible. Compare the result with the seller chart and a reference garment measured in the same way. Otherwise two apparently precise numbers may describe different things.

Suppose an illustrative jacket listing gives a chest width of 60 cm, but a warehouse image seems to show 57 cm. First check whether the garment is flat, whether the tape begins at zero and whether both measurements use underarm-to-underarm width. If those conditions agree, preserve the difference and ask for clarification. If the image is angled or partly folded, request a clearer measurement before treating the apparent difference as a confirmed sizing error.

sections.heading: Separate color uncertainty from a visible variant mismatch
paragraphs: Seller lighting, warehouse lighting, camera processing and your screen can all affect perceived color. Comparing two images is useful for spotting a major inconsistency, but it does not create a calibrated color measurement. A black item where blue was ordered deserves an option check; a slightly warmer shade under different light calls for a more careful description. Ask for a neutral, well-lit view and check any visible option label before reaching a conclusion.

The same discipline helps with shape and proportions. A wide-angle photograph taken close to a shoe can exaggerate one end. Request a view from a consistent distance or a side-on angle if shape is important. Explain the comparison you need to make. Do not describe every photographic difference as a product defect, and do not dismiss a clearly documented wrong option merely because photography can introduce uncertainty.

sections.heading: Turn the review into a timely, documented decision
paragraphs: Keep a short decision record: item and option, evidence checked, confirmed issue or remaining question, next action and the deadline shown for that order. Review the available return or exchange terms in the live account. This article does not establish a universal deadline or eligibility rule. If a potential issue needs further evidence, request it promptly and ask how the unresolved request affects your available options rather than assuming the clock pauses automatically.

When contacting support, send the saved order detail and the smallest photo set that demonstrates the problem. State the action you are requesting and keep the language factual. If the item matches and no material question remains, record the decision before moving to packing. If uncertainty remains, do not let a spreadsheet recommendation or another buyer's photos substitute for evidence about your own item. Your final choice should follow the unit you actually received.

title: Joyagoo Shipping Cost: Budget a Spreadsheet Before Buying
description: Build a Joyagoo shipping budget before ordering spreadsheet finds. Record item costs, domestic freight, estimated weight and box size with a worked example.
sourceNote: Reviewed 13 October 2026. Every numerical example below is hypothetical, not a Joyagoo shipping quote, tariff or recommended declaration. Use current route terms for an actual parcel.
quickFacts: Product price is only one budget line
Keep item weight separate from packed weight
Compare a normal and a bulkier packing scenario
Recheck the live estimate before payment

sections.heading: Make the shortlist affordable before it reaches the warehouse
paragraphs: A spreadsheet can make an inexpensive product easy to find while leaving its delivery cost invisible. Before buying several Joyagoo finds, decide what you can spend on the whole order and reserve room for the parcel stage. A low product price does not establish a low delivered cost. Shoes with boxes, bulky jackets and rigid accessories can affect a parcel differently even when their prices are similar. This guide helps compare candidate purchases before money is committed.

Create one row per exact variant, with quantity, product price, currency, domestic freight, estimated item weight, packaging notes and the date checked. Keep estimates visibly separate from values confirmed by a seller or warehouse. An unknown weight is not zero. Mark it unknown, ask for useful information or test a wider planning range. The spreadsheet becomes more useful when it exposes uncertainty instead of presenting an incomplete total as a bargain.

sections.heading: Separate product costs from parcel costs
paragraphs: Use separate lines for goods, seller-to-warehouse delivery, optional services, international shipping and any destination charges that apply under the current terms. Record discounts only when their conditions are confirmed for the transaction. Do not subtract an advertised coupon from every item or assume that a delivery promotion covers all routes. If two items share one domestic shipment, confirm how the charge is applied before assigning it twice or removing it entirely.

Keep calculations in a consistent currency, and record any conversion rate as an assumption rather than a guaranteed checkout rate. Payment conversion and service charges may make the amount you pay differ from a simple currency calculation. This worksheet is a purchasing comparison, not tax advice or a final invoice. Leave unresolved destination charges as a separate open line and consult the relevant official information before committing to a parcel.

sections.heading: Estimate weight and space as different inputs
paragraphs: Item weight is only the starting point. The outer carton, retail boxes and protective material can add weight and increase dimensions. Record whether a candidate needs its box for protection, whether a rigid component prevents compact packing and whether removing packaging would create a risk you are unwilling to accept. Do not treat the smallest imaginable parcel as the default scenario. It may be physically unrealistic or unsuitable for the item.

For planning, keep both packed mass and outside dimensions. Some routes use the greater of actual and volumetric weight; the divisor and billing increments depend on the route. A general volume calculation multiplies length, width and height and divides by the specified divisor using the required units. It is a comparison input, not the complete shipping price. The live quote can also depend on destination, restrictions, service options and applicable surcharges.

sections.heading: Work through a hypothetical two-scenario example
paragraphs: Suppose a shortlist contains goods totaling 360 CNY, confirmed domestic freight of 24 CNY and a planning allowance of 30 CNY for optional work. The subtotal before international shipping and destination charges is 414 CNY. The 30 CNY allowance is an invented budget assumption, not an official service fee. Do not hide it inside a product price: keeping it separate makes it easy to replace with the real charge when that becomes known.

Now suppose the packed parcel weighs 2.8 kg and measures 35 × 25 × 20 cm. With an illustrative divisor of 6,000, volumetric weight is about 2.92 kg. A bulkier 40 × 30 × 25 cm arrangement gives 5 kg using the same divisor, even if mass stays 2.8 kg. A route that bills the larger value would therefore have different weight inputs for the two scenarios, before its own rounding rules. Neither result is a monetary shipping quote.

sections.heading: Use the live estimator to test the assumptions
paragraphs: Enter the intended destination and the best available parcel information into the current official estimator. Check that the product type and available lines are appropriate for the actual contents. Record the estimate date, route name, weight method, dimensions entered and any conditions shown. Run the normal and bulkier scenarios using comparable settings. Comparing different destinations or different product restrictions can make the apparent saving meaningless.

If the hypothetical normal scenario produces quote A and the bulkier scenario quote B, your planning totals are 414 CNY plus A and unresolved destination charges, or 414 CNY plus B and those charges. Use the actual quoted currency and convert consistently when needed. Do not invent A and B from a universal cost-per-kilogram figure. A route may have a first-weight charge, later increments or thresholds that prevent a straight multiplication from matching its real quote.

sections.heading: Compare adding, removing and replacing one item
paragraphs: Test the effect of the least certain product. If a bulky accessory forces a larger carton, compare the shortlist with and without it. The difference between those estimates is more useful than dividing total shipping equally across every item. A small soft item may use spare space, while one rigid box can change the parcel's entire shape. Record the assumptions behind each comparison so a later warehouse measurement can explain the difference.

Compare alternatives on the same basis: exact variant, required quantity, domestic freight and realistic packing. A cheaper seller price may lose its advantage if the option includes unnecessary packaging or requires a separate domestic shipment. Conversely, a more compact replacement may reduce the uncertain shipping range without changing your intended use. This is a budget decision based on your candidates, not a ranking of sellers or a claim that the cheapest route is always suitable.

sections.heading: Set a buying limit and update it after arrival
paragraphs: Choose a maximum acceptable total and a personal reserve for unresolved costs before paying for the products. The reserve should reflect the information you lack; no fixed percentage works for every order. If only the most optimistic packing assumption fits your budget, pause or reduce the shortlist. A robust plan still works when the final carton is somewhat larger or a service you actually need has a charge. Record which unknown would make you abandon the purchase.

After warehouse arrival, replace estimated item weights with the measurements available, finish the item review and update the parcel assumptions. Compare the live shipping options again before submission. Keep the old estimate for comparison, but use the new evidence for the decision. This closes the loop from product discovery to an affordable order and gives your next spreadsheet shortlist a better starting point without promising a fixed shipping price.
